problem: The sentence says 10.6 μm is absorbed by many non-metals, then lists steel, which is a metal, in the same 'so it cuts ...' clause. A student may read it as claiming steel absorbs 10.6 μm strongly, which is not the reason CO2 lasers cut steel (they cut it with a reactive gas assist).
fix: Write: 'The 10.6 μm light is absorbed strongly by many non-metals, so it cuts wood, cloth and acrylic well. It also cuts steel and welds metal, usually with an oxygen assist.'

problem: 'The gas tube can be long' appears at the end of the Nd:YAG paragraph but talks about the CO2 gas tube. As placed, it reads as if it describes YAG.
fix: Move it to the CO2 paragraph and make the comparison explicit: 'A gas tube can be made much longer than a YAG crystal, which helps raise CO2 output power.'
